---
title: "MBS: Medicare Benefits Schedule"
description: "Information about claims processed for subsidised health services provided to people under the Medicare Benefits Schedule."
---

Information about claims processed for subsidised health services provided to people under the Medicare Benefits Schedule.

*Provides the official schedule of Medicare-subsidised services, items and explanatory material.*

MBSCAT, MBSGROUP and MBSSUBGROUP on the same row give the item's position in the schedule's hierarchy.","dsrc":"AIHW METEOR data element 603645, Service event—Medicare Benefits Schedule (MBS) item identifier, NN[NNN]","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/603645","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Latest mbs item number for the aggregate item.","k":"mbs_item_number","def":"A numeric item number of up to five digits, format NN[NNN], taken from the published Medicare Benefits Schedule. It is the top of a three-level structure, with MBSGROUP one level down and MBSSUBGROUP the finest, and it is the coarsest usable way to separate attendances from pathology, imaging and procedures.","dsrc":"AIHW METEOR value domain 604113, Medicare Benefits Schedule (MBS) category for the item code N[N]","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/604113","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"The categories which represent the service events within the mbs as represented by a code.","k":"mbs_category_code","def":"A one- or two-digit numeric code, format N[N], with ten permissible values running from 1 professional attendances through diagnostic, therapeutic, imaging and pathology services to 10 dental benefits schedule.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METEOR value domain 604113, 'Medicare Benefits Schedule (MBS) category for the item code N[N]', Department of Health; data element 604119 is mapped to variable name MBSCAT in the MBS extract DSS (METEOR 603356)","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/604113","lim":"It classifies the item billed, not who provided the care or who asked for it. PLIDA stores only the trailing number, so this column has to be read together with MBSGROUP to mean anything.","dsrc":"AIHW METEOR data element 604247, Service event—Medicare Benefits Schedule (MBS) subgroup, code ANNNN","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/604247","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The subgroups which represent the service events within the mbs as represented by a code.","k":"mbs_subgroup_number_within_group","def":"A small integer counting subgroups within a group, starting at 1. It appears only from the 2011 MBS tables onward, so a series spanning the earlier tables has to fall back on NUMSERV.","dsrc":"AIHW METEOR data element 610294, Service event—number of Medicare services claimed, total number N","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/610294","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Number of services claimed","k":"medicare_services_claimed_count","def":"A signed integer taking 1 for a valid service submitted or resubmitted, -1 for cancellations and negative adjustments, and 0 for underpayments, substantiations and co-payment adjustments.","p":"2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2022, 2023","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METEOR data element 610294, 'Service event—number of Medicare services claimed, total number N', Department of Health; the MBS extract DSS records 'Variable name = MDV_NUMSERV'","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/610294","lim":"It is not a count of patient encounters, and because it counts incentive and modifier items a single bulk-billed consultation contributes more than one service. This is the field behind published Medicare service counts, and MDV_NUMSERV is its counterpart that includes those items.","dsrc":"AIHW METEOR data element 601800, Service/care provider—number of Medicare services provided, total number N","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/601800","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The total number of medicare services that are provided by a registered medicare service provider for items in the mbs for which a claim has been processed. it does not include services which can only be claimed in conjunction with other items such as bulk-billing incentive items and modifier items.","k":"medicare_services_provided_count","def":"A signed integer with the same three values as the claimed count: 1 for a valid or resubmitted service, -1 for a cancellation or negative adjustment, and 0 for underpayments, substantiations and co-payment adjustments.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METEOR data element 601800, 'Service/care provider—number of Medicare services provided, total number N', Department of Health; the MBS extract DSS records 'Variable name = NUMSERV'","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/601800","lim":"A period total is net of reversals, because the -1 rows cancel earlier claims, so filtering to positive rows inflates the count and filtering out the zeros drops real claim records that still carry dollars in BENPAID and FEECHARGED. The Productivity Commission describes how the ABS builds it: \"The ABS transforms unique identifiers in the original dataset into a Synthetic AEUID, enabling the datasets within PLIDA modules to be connected with one another, while preventing re-identification in the dataset outside of it\". It is the only person-level key on the row, so grouping by it turns claim lines into a patient's service history, with BENPAID, FEECHARGED and NUMSERV summing per person and ITEM, BTOS and MBSCAT saying what was done. Different datasets from one data source carry consistent values, so the column joins the MBS tables to each other, but the Productivity Commission describes every dataset in the PLIDA Modular Product as joined through its own concordance table, so a join to PBS, AIR or any other dataset should be confirmed against those tables rather than assumed, and reaching Census, ATO or Centrelink data means going through the spine linkage file.","dsrc":"Productivity Commission, 'A-PLIDA-nalysis: Using PLIDA for public policy research and reporting', section on the Person Linkage Spine","durl":"https://assets.pc.gov.au/research/completed/plida/plida.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Synthetic MADIP Person ID","k":"PLIDA synthetic person identifier (Agency Entity Unique ID)","def":"An opaque code standing in for the patient's Medicare enrolment identifier, repeated on every claim line for that person and held consistently across the tables from the same source. It follows no published classification and carries no age, sex, location or card information, so there is no finite list to publish and nothing in the value to decode or order.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"Productivity Commission, 'A-PLIDA-nalysis: Using PLIDA for public policy research and reporting', section on the Person Linkage Spine","url":"https://assets.pc.gov.au/research/completed/plida/plida.pdf","lim":"The value cannot be matched against the identifier for the same person in another agency's data, because the Productivity Commission notes that \"Synthetic AEUIDs are unique to an entity within a data source and are not repeated across sources\": an MBS value equal to a Census or ATO value is a coincidence, not a person. It names the patient the service was for, not the person who lodged the claim or paid the account, and not the practitioner, who is SCRAM_SPR when servicing and SCRAM_RPR when referring.
